investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (0/2 schedulable), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remoteState value, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent and the expected-output contract was violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have no remaining VM slots, likely because other remote agent pods or workloads are already consuming all available peer-pod capacity.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector targets only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are saturated; if the selector was recently broadened or narrowed it could explain why 4 nodes are excluded.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for current remote agent demand: the total cluster size (6 nodes, only 2 kata-capable) may be insufficient for the concurrent load of eval probes plus production workloads.

Lower probability — a transient spike in remote agent creation requests (e.g., from other eval runs or user activity) temporarily exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota at the time of the probe window (22:11–22:18 UTC on 2026-06-20).

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T22:13–22:18Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (only 2 nodes carry this resource, both exhausted) and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval's createAgent call cannot schedule a VM-backed pod, the probe never reaches the state-polling stage and produces zero evidence, causing the remote-agent-state contract (requiring orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod submitted by the eval runner (and, by extension, any real remote-agent creation attempt) is left Unschedulable. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so they are not candidates at all. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent before it can collect any evidence, so the check fails before orgId, agentId, readyState, or state can be written, producing a complete contract gap. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader production incident is present in the packet.

No agent was ever created, so the eval runner never reached the runtime chat step and produced zero evidence — all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler could not place the resulting pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained unscheduled for ~134–143 seconds across all three checks before timing out, preventing any agent lifecycle progress and leaving the expected-output contract entirely unsatisfied.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (0/2 schedulable), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remoteState value, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent and the expected-output contract was violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have no remaining VM slots, likely because other remote agent pods or workloads are already consuming all available peer-pod capacity.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector targets only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are saturated; if the selector was recently broadened or narrowed it could explain why 4 nodes are excluded.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for current remote agent demand: the total cluster size (6 nodes, only 2 kata-capable) may be insufficient for the concurrent load of eval probes plus production workloads.

Lower probability — a transient spike in remote agent creation requests (e.g., from other eval runs or user activity) temporarily exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota at the time of the probe window (22:11–22:18 UTC on 2026-06-20).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pods: only 2 nodes carry that resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No agent was ever created, so the eval runner never reached the runtime chat step and produced zero evidence — all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler could not place the resulting pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained unscheduled for ~134–143 seconds across all three checks before timing out, preventing any agent lifecycle progress and leaving the expected-output contract entirely unsatisfied.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/stuck VMs from prior eval runs may have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and any VM slot contention immediately causes total unavailability.

Tertiary — a prior eval run's cleanup did not release kata.peerpods.io/vm resources (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs did not complete successfully), leaving orphaned VM allocations that block new scheduling.

Lower confidence — a cluster-level change reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, shrinking headroom; no source or incident evidence supports this directly.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the production cluster to determine current VM slot utilization and identify any pods from prior eval runs that did not release their allocations.

Search for orphaned or stuck pods in the eval namespace that were created by prior remote-agent status-probe runs and manually terminate any that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources without active eval sessions.

Review the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm that cleanup is reliably invoked even when createAgent or downstream steps throw, and that it releases the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource.

Assess whether the 2-node kata.peerpods.io/vm pool is sufficient for the eval run frequency; if concurrent eval runs or other workloads regularly exhaust the pool, consider expanding the node pool or adding VM slot capacity.

Verify the node affinity/selector configuration on remote-agent pods to confirm that only 2 of 6 nodes are intentionally eligible; if more nodes should be eligible, investigate whether the selector is overly restrictive.
This is an eval-infrastructure failure. Do not escalate as a user-facing incident unless user-traffic or incident signals are separately confirmed.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is persistent or was transient at the time of the original run; a pass on re-run suggests transient exhaustion, a continued fail confirms sustained capacity shortage.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared failure mode
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that all three checks continue to fail with the same Unschedulable message, validating the shared scheduling root cause rather than an isolated runtime issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes show available VM slots at the time of the next eval run and the pod still fails to schedule, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but a different scheduling constraint (e.g., node affinity misconfiguration or quota policy).

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the scheduling layer would not be the shared root cause and the failure would be localized to the runtime chat step.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If cluster node inspection shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was never provisioned on more than 2 nodes and those nodes have available slots, the root cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.
If the eval runner logs show the pod was never submitted to the scheduler (e.g., an API error before pod creation), the Kubernetes scheduling layer would not be the root cause.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity before attempting remote-agent creation, and emits a warning if available slots fall below the number of concurrent remote-agent checks.
Add an eval that detects and reports orphaned remote-agent pods (Running or Terminating beyond a TTL threshold) in the eval namespace, to catch cleanup failures before they exhaust VM capacity.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations return to baseline after each remote-agent eval cycle.
Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create alone at a lower frequency to detect scheduling capacity degradation before the full three-check suite is affected.
